name: Saddle Price
html:
Welcome back reader. We hope that this module of 2D Arrays is helping you learn new concepts.

In this article, we are going to solve The problem of saddle price. The saddle price is defined as the least value in the row and the maximum value in the column.

Important Links : Problem Link, Question Video , Solution Video

Approach :

As any other question, the first step of this question is also taking an input from the user which will be :

  • The dimension of the matrix (Square Matrix)
  • The elements of this matrix

Let us quickly take the input and move forward with the solution.

Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); int[][] arr = new int[n][n]; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) { arr[i][j] = scn.nextInt(); } }
java; true";

The first condition for an element to be a saddle price is that it should be the minimum element in the row and after that we check if it is the maximum element in the column or not.

Let's start solving this problem and don't worry, this is not a difficult problem. Trust me, this is an easy one.

So, let us move step by step. As discussed, the first step is to find the minimum element in the row. Let's work upon that.

Working :

We enter a row and assume that it's first element is the minimum element. Then as we move further in the row, we compare our assumed minimum element with every element and as we encounter a new minimum, we update our minimum.

The extra colno is to remember what was the column number of our minimum element.

for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) //row { min = arr[ i ][ 0 ]; for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) { //columns if(min > arr[i][j]){ min = arr[i][j]; colno = j; } } System.out.print("Minimum element : " + min); System.out.print("Row : " + i); System.out.print("Column : " + colno); }
java; true";

This piece of code prints the minimum element and it's coordinates for every row.

Let's consider that we have found the minimum element of the First row. According to the definition of sadness price, now we need to determine if it is the maximum element of its column.

If yes, then it is the saddle price of this given matrix, else we will have to move to the next row and repeat the same process again. This working is described briefly in the solution video .

Watch video Time Complexity :

In the worst-case scenario we might need to traverse all the elements in the matrix, so the time complexity comes out to be n square (n*n).

Space Complexity :

Since we are using only a handful of variables, space complexity is constant, O( 1 ).

Now, take some time to write this code and come back to take any help you require.

import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); int[][] arr = new int[n][n]; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) { arr[i][j] = scn.nextInt(); } } int colno = 0, min = 0; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { // rows min = arr[i][0]; for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) { // columns if (min > arr[i][j]) { min = arr[i][j]; colno = j; } } boolean potentialAns = true; for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) { if (min < arr[r][colno]) { potentialAns = false; break; } } if (potentialAns == true) { System.out.print(min); return; } } System.out.print("Invalid Input"); } }
java; true";

Let's go through the code once.

After taking input, using a loop('i') we parse every row.

ROW

  1. The minimum element comes out to be 11.Now, min contains 11 and colno contains 0. By marking potentailAns = true, we assume that this min could be the saddle price. We traverse every element in the column of min ( colno = 0 ), to check if it is the maximum element in its column. Since, 11 is not the highest element in this column, we break out of the loop, marking potentailAns = false. (that 11 is not our potential answer.)

ROW

  1. The minimum element comes out to be 21.Now, min = 21 and colno = 0. We mark potentailAns = true and assume that this min could be the saddle price. We traverse every element in the column of min ( colno = 0 ), to check if it is the maximum element in its column. Since, 21 is not the highest element in this column, we break out of the loop, marking potentailAns = false. (that 21 is not saddle price.)

ROW

  1. The process is exactly the same for this row. Give it a try yourself, I am sure you will be able to do this.

ROW

  1. The minimum element comes out to be 41.Now, min = 11 and colno = 0. We mark potentailAns = true assuming that this min could be the saddle price. We traverse every element in the column of min ( colno = 0 ), to check if it is the maximum element in its column.

Since, 41 is the highest element in this column,thus we don't enter the if condition. Our potentailAns = true, thus we print the saddle price and return.

And VOILA!! This is how we have to find the saddle price. Since, there is a possibility that a matrix might not contain a saddle price, in that case, we come out of all the loops and at the last we print "invalid input"

The whole process and the code is explained in the solution video from 2:10 - 8:20.

Watch video

Now, there is a fun fact, that in a matrix there can never be more than 1 saddle price.

Let's see how.

In the given figure, we have assumed that we have 2 saddle prices i.e. H and J. Since they are saddle prices, they are smallest in the row and largest in the column.


Thus, H is greater than F, which is a row element and smaller than L, which is another column element. Same for J, J > F and J < L. Putting the 2 inequalities of H together we get, L < H < F ? L < F. And similarly putting together the 2 inequalities of J we get, F < J < L ? F < L.

Thus, H is greater than F, which is a row element and smaller than L, which is another column element. Same for J, J > F and J < L. Putting the 2 inequalities of H together we get, L < H < F ? L < F. And similarly putting together the 2 inequalities of J we get, F < J < L ? F < L.
